The Prado brings together works by Velázquez, Goya and Hieronymus Bosch. Discover their paintings and the creatures they inspired.

Velázquez depicts Infanta Margarita with her attendants in the Alcázar of Madrid. The painter is at work on the left, and a mirror reflects the king and queen in the background.
The Garden of Earthly Delights
Hieronymus Bosch
Bosch’s triptych brings together paradise, a world of fantastic figures and animals, and a vision of hell. Its scenes are full of small details.
Picasso painted this work in 1937. Its figures and shades of white, black and grey express the suffering and violence of war.
Figure at a Window
Dalí paints his sister Anna Maria from behind as she looks out over the sea from a window in Cadaqués. The blue light and her stillness give the scene a quiet mood.
Young Knight in a Landscape
A young man in armour holds his sword in a landscape full of plants and animals. The ermine and the inscriptions hint at the knight’s honour and virtues.
Hotel Room
A traveller sits on the edge of a bed reading a train timetable, with her luggage beside her. The lines of the room and the harsh light emphasise her isolation.
The Starry Night
A sky filled with stars and swirls hangs over a village at the foot of the mountains. Van Gogh painted this imagined view in Saint-Rémy in 1889, with a large cypress in the foreground.
The Persistence of Memory
Several soft clocks droop over a branch and other surfaces in an almost empty landscape. Dalí combines familiar objects and unusual shapes in a dreamlike scene.
Sunflowers
A vase holds sunflowers at different stages of life, painted in many shades of yellow. This 1889 version belongs to the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam.
Almond Blossom
Almond branches bloom against a blue sky. Van Gogh painted the work in 1890 as a gift for his brother Theo and sister-in-law Jo after their son was born.
The Birth of Venus
The wind carries Venus to shore on a shell, while a figure approaches with a cloak. Botticelli turns a story from classical mythology into an image of ideal beauty.
Primavera
Nine figures from mythology gather in a garden of orange trees and flowers. Venus stands at the centre, with Cupid above and the Three Graces dancing to her left.
The Scream
A figure holds both hands to its head under a rippling red sky. The lines and colours convey anguish. This is the version painted around 1910 and held by MUNCH.
A woman with closed eyes is surrounded by curving lines and a red halo. Munch uses colour and shape to express emotion. This 1894 version belongs to MUNCH.
The Creation of Adam
Michelangelo
God reaches out to Adam, their fingers almost touching. The scene is one of the frescoes Michelangelo painted on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
The School of Athens
Raphael
Plato and Aristotle talk at the centre of a monumental hall, surrounded by thinkers from antiquity. This fresco decorates the Room of the Segnatura in the Vatican.
The Great Wave off Kanagawa
A giant wave curls over several boats, while Mount Fuji looks small in the distance. The print is part of the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.
Washington Crossing the Delaware
George Washington travels by boat among blocks of ice during the American War of Independence. Leutze painted this idealised version of the Delaware River crossing in 1851.
Mona Lisa
Leonardo portrays Lisa Gherardini seated in front of a distant landscape. The soft outlines of the sfumato technique and her subtle smile make this one of the Louvre’s best-known works.
Liberty Leading the People
A figure representing Liberty raises the French flag and leads a group over a barricade. Delacroix drew inspiration from the July Revolution of 1830 in Paris.
